title: Nightly: history, triage, mutation and the locks
bridge: The nightly history is like the flaky-test view in a CI dashboard: one row per test, one column per night. Except: we build it ourselves from JUnit files, and people act on it. They fix, quarantine with a ticket, or hand off, so that a red night means something again.
intro: The cloud nightly has failed its last 60 scheduled runs, so nobody reads it. This lesson records per-test results and triages the failures. It adds a mutation report on agent-changed files and takes branch pushes off the QA locks. The test code is Python because it lives in fcp's Django backend; the rest is workflow YAML.

picture.caption: Nightly results become a table, the table becomes decisions, and branch pushes stop waiting for QA.

nodes.label: FCP Lab smoke on branch pushes

steps.text: kubectl cp copies junit.xml out of the pod; upload-artifact keeps it 90 days
nightly_history.py downloads 20 nights and writes pass, fail or rerun-pass per test
each failing or rerun-only test gets a category, an owner and an action
the next job mutates yesterday's agent-changed files, judged by the API layer
branch pushes run the Lab; QA keeps main, the nightly and releases

sections.h: Keep a JUnit file per night (G7-24)
p: The baseline, read on 12 Oct: "[CLOUD] - Integration Tests" (cloud-int-tests-dispatch.yml, 02:44 UTC) failed its last 60 scheduled runs. The 12 Oct AWS run had 4 failed, 312 passed and 4 reruns in 88 minutes. Today a failed night is a Slack message and an 88-minute log.

The tests run inside a Kubernetes pod through kubectl exec. So the change is in _cloud-int-tests-reusable-aws.yml and -gcp.yml. Add -rR --junitxml=/tmp/junit.xml to the entrypoint call, then copy the file out before the pod is deleted. -rR lists the tests that passed only after a rerun.
sections.because: We copy the report out before "Delete the integration tests pod", because the file lives inside the pod and dies with it.

code.text:
# In "Run Integration Tests", add to the entrypoint call inside `kubectl exec`:
      #   integration-tests-entrypoint-ci.sh -s --durations=0 -vv --color=yes -rR --junitxml=/tmp/junit.xml ...
      # Then, before "Delete the integration tests pod":
      - name: Copy the JUnit report out of the integration tests pod
        if: always() && inputs.run_nightly_tests
        continue-on-error: true
        run: >
          kubectl cp -c integration-tests
          "${{ needs.prepare_cloud_environment.outputs.pod_with_sdk }}:/tmp/junit.xml" junit-aws.xml
      - name: Keep it for the nightly history
        if: always() && inputs.run_nightly_tests
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: nightly-junit-aws
          path: junit-aws.xml
          retention-days: 90
      # scripts/nightly_history.py then reads the last 20 scheduled runs:
      #   gh run list --workflow cloud-int-tests-dispatch.yml --event schedule -L 20 --json databaseId
      #   gh run download <id> -n nightly-junit-aws
      # and writes nightly-history.md: one row per test, one column per night (pass / fail / rerun-pass).

p: scripts/nightly_history.py runs gh run list --workflow cloud-int-tests-dispatch.yml --event schedule -L 20 to find the last 20 scheduled runs. For each run it calls gh run download <id> -n nightly-junit-aws and reads the XML. It writes nightly-history.md: test by night, with pass, fail or rerun-pass, newest night first.

Ten tests already carry @pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=N), for example in gc/test_gc.py and rhino_sdk/test_metrics/. A test that passed after a rerun counts as flaky, not green. The BE flaky-test fixer (G5) reads the same data later. Do the same for the frontend nightly with Playwright's JUnit reporter, but cloud first.

sections.h: Triage: four categories, one owner each (G7-29)
p: A nightly that is never green teaches everyone to ignore it. G7-29 is one session with the BE guild over nightly-history.md. Each failing or rerun-only test gets a category and an owner.

Real bug or test bug: fix it now if it takes under an hour; otherwise open a Jira bug with the output. Environment: hand it to DevOps with the evidence, such as the 12 Oct instant-container failure in rhino_sdk/test_code_object.py. Flaky: quarantine it with a Jira ticket labelled flaky-test for the G5 fixer.

The 10 existing flaky(reruns=N) markers get flaky-test tickets too, so their flakiness shows in the history instead of being retried away. Post one line a week in #integration-tests-nightly: green nights out of the last 7.

callout.text: People quarantine tests; agents never quarantine, skip or delete them. The weakened-tests check (G0) fails an agent PR that does.

p: A quarantined test keeps running and reporting, but it does not turn the nightly red. The trick is a non-strict xfail: pytest expects the test may fail. If it fails, junit.xml shows it as skipped with the reason; if it passes, nothing breaks. Register the marker in cloud/rhinoCloud/pytest.ini.
sections.because: We turn quarantine into xfail at collection time, because then every quarantined test carries its ticket into the report.

code.text:
# Called from the existing pytest_collection_modifyitems (which already shuffles tests and adds trace ids).
# Register the marker in cloud/rhinoCloud/pytest.ini:
#   quarantine(ticket): known flaky; still runs and reports, but does not turn the nightly red


def _apply_quarantine(items: list[pytest.Item]) -> None:
    for item in items:
        marker = item.get_closest_marker("quarantine")
        if marker is None:
            continue
        ticket = marker.kwargs["ticket"]  # required: every quarantined test has a Jira ticket and an owner
        # Non-strict xfail: the test still runs; junit.xml shows it as skipped with this reason, so
        # scripts/nightly_history.py can list quarantined tests and their tickets.
        item.add_marker(pytest.mark.xfail(reason=f"quarantined, see {ticket}", strict=False))


# In a test module, added by a person after triage (agents never quarantine, skip or delete tests):
#
#   @pytest.mark.quarantine(ticket="RH-0000")  # placeholder key
#   def test_...(api_client): ...
#
# The 10 tests with @pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=N) today get a flaky-test ticket each; decide with the guild
# whether to replace their reruns with quarantine, so the flakiness shows in the history.

p: A suite that passes no matter what the code does gives agents false confidence. A mutation tool changes the code on purpose, and each change is a mutant (lesson p10-5). If the tests still pass, the mutant survived and the code is weakly tested. Meta's ACH work used surviving mutants this way.
G7-35 runs mutmut every night on the cloud files that agent PRs changed the day before, at most 10. It is advisory: never a required check.
sections.because: We pick only yesterday's agent-changed files, because mutation testing is slow and those are the files we most need to trust.

code.text:
name: "[CLOUD] - Mutation report (advisory)"
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 4 * * *' # after the 02:44 UTC cloud nightly

jobs:
  mutation:
    runs-on: fcp-runner-set
    # services and env: the same Postgres service and env as the API Tests job in cloud-ci.yml
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Cloud files that agent PRs changed yesterday
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh pr list --state merged --limit 50 --search "author:app/rhino-ai-agents merged:>=$(date -u -d yesterday +%F)" \
            --json files --jq '.[].files[].path' \
            | grep -E '^cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/.+\.py$' | grep -vE '/(tests|migrations|integration-tests)/' \
            | sed 's|^cloud/rhinoCloud/||' | sort -u | head -n 10 > touched.txt || true

sections.h: Mutation report, part 2: mutate and publish
p: Only the API layer judges the mutants, because rhinoCore/tests run on manage.py test, not pytest. Check one thing first: that mutmut 3's mutants/ copy is what rhinoCloud.rhinoCore imports, since the code is imported through PYTHONPATH=cloud. If it is not, run from cloud/ with rhinoCloud/... paths, or try cosmic-ray, and say which in the PR.
The weekly run review reads the report. The G5 coverage-gap routine turns survivors into test proposals.
sections.because: We write mutmut's config at run time, because the files to mutate change every night.

code.text:
- name: Mutate only those files; only the API layer judges the mutants
        working-directory: cloud/rhinoCloud
        run: |
          [ -s ../../touched.txt ] || { echo "No agent-changed cloud files yesterday"; exit 0; }
          printf '[mutmut]\npaths_to_mutate=%s\ntests_dir=tests_api/\n' "$(paste -sd, ../../touched.txt)" > setup.cfg
          uv run --frozen --group api-tests --with mutmut mutmut run || true
          uv run --frozen --group api-tests --with mutmut mutmut results > ../../mutation-report.txt
      - name: Report (advisory, never a required check)
        if: hashFiles('mutation-report.txt') != ''
        run: |
          { echo "## Surviving mutants in agent-changed files"; echo '```'; cat mutation-report.txt; echo '```'; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: hashFiles('mutation-report.txt') != ''
        with: { name: mutation-report, path: mutation-report.txt }

sections.h: Take branch pushes off the QA locks (G7-31)
p: Every cloud or client branch push waits 20 to 30 minutes on cloud_integration_tests_{aws,gcp} or client_integration_tests_{aws,gcp}. Agents push often, so this queue would grow with them. G7-31 runs QA integration jobs only on main, in the nightly and for releases. Branch pushes get the Lab smoke instead.

Do not move on day one. Run the Lab smoke next to QA for two weeks (G7-26) and compare the verdicts push by push. Move only when the Lab caught everything QA caught, and keep the exceptions (for example GCP-only paths) on the nightly. The dispatch workflows keep their concurrency groups, which still protect each QA environment.
sections.because: We change only the if: of the QA jobs, because publish already needs both of them on main, so post-merge QA stays.

code.text:
lab-images:
    needs: check-changes
    if: github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' && needs.check-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_lab-images-reusable.yml
    secrets: inherit

  lab-smoke:
    name: FCP Lab smoke
    needs: [check-changes, lab-images]
    if: github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' && needs.check-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_lab-smoke-reusable.yml
    with:
      image_tag: ${{ needs.lab-images.outputs.tag }}
    secrets: inherit

  integration-tests-aws:
    name: "I&T - AWS"
    needs: [build, build-rhino-agent, check-changes]
    # Shared QA (lock cloud_integration_tests_aws on qa-cloud / rhino-agent-qa-1) only after merge to main.
    # The nightly (cloud-int-tests-dispatch.yml) and releases keep using it; branch pushes no longer wait for it.
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_cloud-int-tests-reusable-aws.yml
    # with: ...unchanged

  # integration-tests-gcp: the same `if:`. `publish` already needs both and only runs on main.

quiz.q: A nightly test failed once and passed on its rerun. How does the history count it?

options.text: As rerun-pass, which the triage treats as flaky, not green.
options.why: -rR lists reruns, and passed-after-rerun is flaky by the G7-24 rule.

options.text: As pass, because the final result was green.
options.why: That is how flakiness gets retried away; the history keeps it visible.

options.text: As fail, because the first attempt failed.
options.why: It is its own category, so triage can see flakiness apart from real failures.

quiz.q: An agent's PR adds @pytest.mark.quarantine(ticket="RH-1234") to a failing test. What should happen?

options.text: It is fine, because the marker has a ticket.
options.why: People quarantine after triage; agents never quarantine, skip or delete tests.

options.text: The weakened-tests check fails the PR; only a person quarantines.
options.why: This is a wall: agents never change the checks they are judged by.

options.text: The nightly ignores the marker for agent PRs.
options.why: The nightly does not know who added the marker; the PR check does.

quiz.q: Why does G7-31 keep QA running on main?

options.text: Because publish needs both QA jobs, and post-merge QA stays a safety net.
options.why: Only branch pushes move to the Lab; main, the nightly and releases keep QA.

options.text: Because the Lab cannot run on main.
options.why: It could; the plan keeps QA there on purpose.

options.text: Because the QA locks only exist on main.
options.why: The locks exist for every run; that is why branches waited for them.
